q: A Pay and Accounts Office effects a recovery on behalf of another Pay and Accounts Office and the amount awaits settlement between the two offices. Pending final adjustment in the books of the office on whose behalf the recovery was made, the transaction is initially accounted for under:

options.B: Pay and Accounts Office Suspense under Major Head 8658

e: A recovery effected by one Pay and Accounts Office on behalf of another, pending settlement between the offices, is initially accounted for under Pay and Accounts Office Suspense, Minor Head 101 under Major Head 8658.

q: In the Government system of accounts, cheques issued by Government offices and remaining unpaid, and similar items, are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Cheques issued by Government offices and remaining unpaid, and similar items, are accounted for under Major Head 8670 Cheques and Bills in the Public Account of India.

q: The link head 'Deposits with Reserve Bank', through which the cash transactions of Railways with the Government account at the Reserve Bank are adjusted, is Major Head:
e: The link head Deposits with Reserve Bank, through which the cash transactions of Railways with the Government account at the Reserve Bank are adjusted, is Major Head 8675.

q: Cash remittances and adjustments between officers rendering accounts to the same Accounts Officer are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Cash remittances and adjustments between officers rendering accounts to the same Accounts Officer are accounted for under Major Head 8782 Cash Remittances and Adjustments between Officers rendering accounts to the same Accountant General.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Major Head 8786 is the Adjusting Account between Central and State Governments.
2. Major Head 8787 is the Adjusting Account with Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: In the List of Major and Minor Heads, Major Head 8786 is the Adjusting Account between Central and State Governments and Major Head 8787 is the Adjusting Account with Railways, so both statements are correct.

q: The balances of the several departments and accounting circles with one another, pending adjustment, are watched in the Government accounts under Major Head:
e: Departmental Balances, under Major Head 8671, is the head under which the balances of the several departments and accounting circles with one another, pending adjustment, are watched in the Government accounts.

q: The Railway Convention Committee consists of a total of:
e: The Railway Convention Committee consists of 18 members in all - 12 from the Lok Sabha and 6 from the Rajya Sabha.

q: The members of the Railway Convention Committee are nominated in the following manner:

options.A: All members are nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.B: All members are elected by proportional representation
options.C: All members are nominated by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
options.D: The Lok Sabha members are nominated by the Speaker and the Rajya Sabha members are nominated by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

e: The members of the Railway Convention Committee are nominated, not elected: the Lok Sabha members by the Speaker and the Rajya Sabha members by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

q: The Chairperson of the Railway Convention Committee is appointed:

options.B: By the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, from amongst the members of the Committee
options.D: By the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

e: The Chairperson of the Railway Convention Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Convention Committee is constituted on the basis of a resolution adopted by the Lok Sabha and concurred in by the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Railway Convention Committee is a statutory body constituted under the Railways Act, 1989.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Railway Convention Committee is constituted on the basis of a resolution adopted by the Lok Sabha and concurred in by the Rajya Sabha, so statement 1 is correct; it is not a statutory body under the Railways Act, 1989, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: Besides reviewing the rate of dividend payable by Railways to General Revenues, the Railway Convention Committee also reviews and makes recommendations on:

options.A: The audit objections raised by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: The fare and freight structure of passenger and goods services
options.C: The level of appropriations to the various railway funds, such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund, Capital Fund and Pension Fund
options.D: The Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways before they are voted

e: Besides reviewing the rate of dividend payable by Railways to General Revenues, the Railway Convention Committee reviews and recommends on the level of appropriations to the railway funds such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund, Capital Fund and Pension Fund.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Accounts of the Union Government in the format introduced from 2014-15:
1. Volume I presents the financial statements of the Government in summarised form.
2. Volume II presents the detailed financial statements.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: In the format introduced from 2014-15, the Finance Accounts of the Union Government are in two volumes: Volume I presents the financial statements in summarised form and Volume II presents the detailed statements, so both statements are correct.

q: In Volume I of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government, Statement No. 9 is the statement of:

options.C: Loans and advances given by the Government

e: In Volume I of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government, Statement No. 9 is the Statement of Guarantees given by the Government, in the sequence where Statement 7 covers loans and advances and Statement 8 covers investments.

q: A separate statement showing the distribution of the expenditure of the Union Government between voted and charged expenditure forms part of the:
e: Statement No. 11 of Volume I of the Finance Accounts is the statement of voted and charged expenditure, showing the distribution of Union expenditure between voted and charged, so this statement forms part of the Finance Accounts.

q: In Volume I of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government, the Statement of Progressive Capital Expenditure is:
e: In Volume I of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government, the Statement of Progressive Capital Expenditure is Statement No. 5, following Statement 3 on receipts and Statement 4 on expenditure of the Consolidated Fund.

q: The Combined Finance and Revenue Accounts, consolidating the accounting information contained in the Finance Accounts of the Union and of the State Governments, are prepared by:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: The Combined Finance and Revenue Accounts, consolidating the Finance Accounts of the Union and the State Governments, are prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

q: In Volume I of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government, Statement No. 1 is the:

options.C: Statement of Borrowings and other Liabilities
options.D: Summary of Balances under the Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund and Public Account

e: In Volume I of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government, Statement No. 1 is the Statement of Financial Position; Statement No. 2 is Receipts and Disbursements and Statement No. 13 is the Summary of Balances.

q: Under the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the preparation and submission by the CAG of the accounts relating to the annual receipts and disbursements of the Union and of the States to the President, the Governors and the Administrators concerned is dealt with in:
e: Section 11 of the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 deals with the preparation and submission by the CAG of the accounts of annual receipts and disbursements of the Union and the States to the President, Governors and Administrators concerned.

q: The duty of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India to give information to, and render assistance to, the Union and the States in connection with their accounts is provided for in the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:
e: Section 12 of the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 provides for the duty of the CAG to give information to, and render assistance to, the Union and the States in connection with their accounts.

q: The laying of the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in relation to the accounts of Government companies and corporations before Parliament or the State Legislature, as the case may be, is provided for in the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:
e: Section 19A of the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 provides for laying the CAG reports relating to the accounts of Government companies and corporations before Parliament or the State Legislature, as the case may be.

q: The power of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India to dispense with detailed audit of any accounts, or class of transactions, in accordance with the provisions of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 is contained in:
e: Section 24 of the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 contains the power of the CAG to dispense with detailed audit of any accounts or class of transactions.

q: Section 21 of the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 relates to:

options.A: The power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act
options.B: The power to make regulations by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The repeal of the earlier enactments on the subject
options.D: The delegation of the powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Section 21 of the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 relates to the delegation of the powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India to officers of his department.

q: In performance audit, 'efficiency' of an activity or programme is concerned mainly with the relationship between:

options.A: The results achieved and the objectives originally laid down for the programme
options.B: The goods or services produced and the resources used to produce them, that is, whether the inputs have been used optimally
options.C: The expenditure incurred and the provision made in the grant for the purpose
options.D: The receipts realised and the receipts estimated in the Budget

e: In performance audit, efficiency concerns the relationship between the goods or services produced and the resources used to produce them, that is whether inputs have been used optimally to obtain the outputs.

q: In performance audit, 'effectiveness' of a programme is judged mainly by:

options.A: Whether the expenditure on the programme was sanctioned by the competent authority
options.B: Whether the accounts of the programme have been correctly maintained
options.C: The extent to which the programme has achieved the objectives and the intended results laid down for it
options.D: Whether the inputs of the programme were procured at the lowest rates

e: In performance audit, effectiveness is judged by the extent to which a programme has achieved the objectives and intended results laid down for it, as distinct from economy of inputs or efficiency of their use.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Propriety audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is discretionary in nature.
2. Compliance (regularity) audit, verifying conformity of expenditure with the Constitution, laws, rules and sanctions, is an obligatory duty of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Propriety audit by the CAG is discretionary, while compliance or regularity audit verifying conformity of expenditure with the Constitution, laws, rules and sanctions is an obligatory duty of the CAG, so both statements are correct.

q: In the audit of secret service expenditure, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

options.A: Accepts the certificate of the competent authority that the expenditure has been incurred, without demanding detailed vouchers for the expenditure
options.B: Conducts a cent-per-cent check of every voucher of the expenditure
options.C: Refuses to include such expenditure in the accounts altogether
options.D: Refers every case of such expenditure to the Public Accounts Committee

e: For secret service expenditure, the CAG accepts the certificate of the competent authority that the expenditure has been incurred and does not demand detailed vouchers, because of the secret nature of the expenditure.

q: The Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India which comments upon the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts of the Union Government is the Report on:
e: The CAG Report on Union Government Accounts is the report which comments upon the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts of the Union Government.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The losses sustained by Railways on essential commodities carried below the cost of operation form part of the Social Service Obligations of Railways.
2. The losses sustained by Railways on the operation of uneconomic branch lines form part of the Social Service Obligations of Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Social Service Obligations of Railways include both the losses on essential commodities carried below the cost of operation and the losses on operation of uneconomic branch lines, so both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following does NOT form part of the Social Service Obligations of Indian Railways?

options.A: Losses on passenger and other coaching services rendered below cost
options.B: Losses on essential commodities carried below the cost of operation
options.C: Losses on the operation of uneconomic branch lines
options.D: Losses on the operation of strategic lines maintained for purposes of national defence

e: Losses on strategic lines maintained for national defence are borne as a defence-related obligation and are not counted among the Social Service Obligations of Railways, which cover coaching losses, essential commodities carried below cost and uneconomic branch lines.

q: On Indian Railways, the losses incurred on passenger and other coaching services are largely made good out of the surplus earnings of freight traffic. This practice is an instance of:
e: Making good the losses on passenger and coaching services out of the surplus earnings of freight traffic is cross-subsidisation, where earnings of one service subsidise the below-cost operation of another.

q: The component of the Extra Budgetary Resources of Railways described as institutional finance refers to:

options.A: Borrowings raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation in the market against rolling stock
options.B: Long-term funds raised from institutional sources such as insurance and pension funds and multilateral and bilateral agencies for railway projects, to be serviced through the incremental revenues of the projects
options.C: The investment made by private parties in railway projects under public-private partnership
options.D: The Gross Budgetary Support provided to Railways through the Union Budget

e: In Railway EBR, institutional finance means long-term funds raised from institutional sources such as insurance and pension funds and multilateral and bilateral agencies for railway projects, serviced through the incremental revenues of the projects.

q: A port-connectivity railway line is executed through a joint venture in which a private party contributes equity and bears a part of the project cost. In the financing of the Railway Plan, this private investment is classified as part of:
e: Private investment in a railway project through a joint venture or PPP is classified in Railway Plan financing as part of Extra Budgetary Resources, being neither Gross Budgetary Support nor internal resources of Railways.

q: Under the Separation Convention of 1924, the definite annual contribution payable by Railways to the General Revenues was to be:

options.A: Paid only in years in which Railways earned a surplus
options.B: The first charge on the net receipts of Railways
options.C: Met out of the Railway Reserve Fund
options.D: Fixed by the Finance Commission every five years

e: Under the Separation Convention of 1924, the definite annual contribution payable by Railways to General Revenues was the first charge on the net receipts of Railways.

q: For new lines in backward areas, which of the following reliefs was suggested to facilitate their construction, as noted in the Ninth Report (1973) of the Railway Convention Committee on Social Burdens?

options.A: Exemption of such lines from audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Making land for such lines available free of cost and exemption from dividend liability during construction and for a specified period after opening
options.C: Meeting the entire working expenses of such lines from the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Charging the losses of such lines to the States in which the lines are situated

e: As noted in the Ninth Report (1973) of the Railway Convention Committee on Social Burdens, reliefs suggested for new lines in backward areas included making land available free of cost and exemption from dividend liability during construction and for a specified period after opening.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before the separation of Railway finances in 1924-25, the finances of Railways formed part of the general finances of the Government of India.
2. Before 1924-25, Railways presented a separate Budget to the Legislature and maintained their own reserve funds out of their surplus.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Before separation in 1924-25, Railway finances formed part of the general finances of the Government of India, so statement 1 is correct; Railways did not then present a separate Budget or maintain their own reserve funds, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: The periodic repairs and repainting of an existing station building, involving no addition to, or improvement of, the asset, are charged in the railway accounts to:
e: Periodic repairs and repainting of an existing station building, with no addition or improvement to the asset, are revenue expenditure and are charged as ordinary working expenses, not to Capital or to the Capital Fund.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Whether expenditure is of a capital nature or of a revenue nature does not depend merely on the amount involved in the expenditure.
2. Ordinary repairs incurred to keep an existing asset in working condition are revenue expenditure.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Capital or revenue nature of expenditure does not depend merely on the amount involved but on its nature and purpose, and ordinary repairs to keep an existing asset in working condition are revenue expenditure, so both statements are correct.

q: In the classification of Government accounts, the Object Heads classify the expenditure according to:

options.A: The function or programme of the Government to which the expenditure relates
options.B: The nature or object of the expenditure, such as salaries, wages, travel expenses and the like
options.C: The department which incurs the expenditure
options.D: The source from which the funds for the expenditure are drawn

e: Object Heads classify expenditure according to the nature or object of the expenditure, such as salaries, wages and travel expenses, at the lowest tier of the six-tier classification of Government accounts.

q: Moneys collected by Government offices and remitted into banks or treasuries, pending their credit to the Government account, are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Moneys collected by Government offices and remitted into banks or treasuries, pending credit to the Government account, are accounted for under Major Head 8677 Remittances into Banks and Treasuries.

q: Minor Head 107 under Major Head 8658 – Suspense Accounts is:
e: Minor Head 107 under Major Head 8658 Suspense Accounts is the Cash Settlement Suspense Account, used for cash settlement of transactions between accounting authorities.

q: The Annual Financial Statement presented to Parliament is, in substance, a statement of:

options.A: The audited receipts and expenditure of the previous financial year
options.B: The estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for a financial year
options.C: The grants voted by the Lok Sabha during the previous session
options.D: The debt position of the Government of India at the close of the year

e: The Annual Financial Statement under Article 112 is in substance a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for a financial year, not of audited past figures.

q: Part A of the Budget Speech of the Finance Minister deals mainly with:

options.A: The taxation proposals of the Government for the ensuing year
options.B: The Demands for Grants of the individual Ministries
options.C: An overview of the economy and the policy initiatives of the Government
options.D: The appropriations charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Part A of the Budget Speech of the Finance Minister gives an overview of the economy and the policy initiatives of the Government; the taxation proposals are dealt with in Part B of the speech.

q: A Vote of Credit granted by the Lok Sabha is sometimes described as a 'blank cheque' to the executive because:

options.A: It is granted as a lump sum for a demand whose magnitude or indefinite character does not permit the details ordinarily given in the Annual Financial Statement to be stated
options.B: It can be drawn upon by the executive without any limit whatsoever
options.C: It does not require the subsequent passing of an Appropriation Act
options.D: It is granted by the President without reference to Parliament

e: A Vote of Credit under Article 116 is called a blank cheque because it is granted as a lump sum for a demand whose magnitude or indefinite character, such as war, does not permit the details ordinarily given in the Annual Financial Statement to be stated.

q: One of the functions of the Estimates Committee of Parliament is to examine:

options.A: Whether the Action Taken Notes on Audit Paras have been furnished in time
options.B: Whether the Government companies are managed on sound commercial principles
options.C: The rate of return on the capital-at-charge of Railways
options.D: Whether the money is well laid out within the limits of the policy implied in the estimates

e: A function of the Estimates Committee is to examine whether the money is well laid out within the limits of the policy implied in the estimates, and to suggest economies and alternative policies.

q: While examining the accounts of the Government, the Public Accounts Committee is required to satisfy itself, among other things, that:

options.A: The estimates for the ensuing year have been framed on a realistic basis
options.B: The expenditure conforms to the authority which governs it
options.C: The undertakings are run in accordance with prudent commercial practices
options.D: The form in which the estimates are presented to Parliament is appropriate

e: The Public Accounts Committee must satisfy itself, among other things, that the expenditure shown in the accounts conforms to the authority which governs it, that is it was legally available and applied to the purpose intended by Parliament.

q: The Committee on Government Assurances of the Lok Sabha examines:

options.A: The rules and regulations framed under delegated legislation
options.B: The reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to public undertakings
options.C: The assurances, promises and undertakings given by Ministers on the floor of the House and reports on the extent to which they have been implemented
options.D: The petitions presented to the Lok Sabha by the public

e: The Committee on Government Assurances of the Lok Sabha examines the assurances, promises and undertakings given by Ministers on the floor of the House and reports on the extent to which they have been implemented.

q: In performance audit, the element of 'economy' is concerned mainly with:

options.A: Acquiring inputs of the appropriate quality and quantity at the least cost
options.B: The relationship between the outputs produced and the inputs consumed
options.C: The extent to which the objectives of the programme have been achieved
options.D: The conformity of expenditure with the applicable rules and sanctions

e: In performance audit, economy is concerned with acquiring inputs of the appropriate quality and quantity at the least cost, minimising the cost of resources used for an activity.

q: A performance audit of a programme finds that the programme has fully achieved its stated targets, but the inputs for it were procured at costs far higher than those incurred by comparable units for inputs of the same quality. The deficiency noticed by Audit relates mainly to:
e: The programme achieved its targets, so effectiveness is not in question; procuring inputs at costs far higher than comparable units for the same quality is a failure of economy, which concerns acquiring inputs at the least cost.

q: In a financial (attest) audit, an unqualified (clean) opinion is expressed when the auditor concludes that:

options.A: The financial statements contain misstatements which are material but not pervasive
options.B: The financial statements present a true and fair view, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework
options.C: Sufficient appropriate evidence could not be obtained for a part of the accounts
options.D: The programme audited has achieved all its objectives economically

e: An unqualified or clean opinion is expressed when the auditor concludes that the financial statements present a true and fair view, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.

q:
Consider the following statements about an 'Emphasis of Matter' paragraph in an audit report:
1. It draws attention to a matter already appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements, and the auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of that matter.
2. It has the same effect as a qualified opinion on the financial statements.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph only draws attention to a matter already appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements and does not modify the auditor opinion, so statement 1 is correct and statement 2, equating it with a qualified opinion, is wrong.

q: 'Audit sampling', as applied in the audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, means:

options.A: Checking every transaction of the audited unit without exception
options.B: Checking only the transactions pointed out by the audited office
options.C: Applying audit procedures to less than the whole of a population of transactions, selected in such a way that the results can be evaluated for the population as a whole
options.D: Checking the accounts of only one month in the year in full

e: Audit sampling means applying audit procedures to less than the whole population of transactions, selected so that all sampling units have a chance of selection and the results can be evaluated for the population as a whole.

q: 'Concurrent audit' of transactions means audit which is conducted:

options.A: Only after the accounts of the financial year have been closed
options.B: At or about the time the transactions take place, on a continuing basis
options.C: Only of the accounts of the headquarters office
options.D: Jointly by the internal audit and the statutory audit at the close of the year

e: Concurrent audit is audit conducted at or about the time the transactions take place, on a continuing basis, unlike post-audit carried out after the accounts of the year have closed.

q: A 'forensic audit' is distinguished from an ordinary audit mainly in that it is conducted:

options.A: Only of the accounts of Government companies
options.C: Before the transactions are entered into by the audited entity
options.D: To detect fraud and irregularities, in a manner whose findings can be used as evidence in legal proceedings

e: A forensic audit is distinguished by its purpose of detecting fraud and irregularities through an investigation conducted so that its findings can be used as evidence in legal proceedings.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Accounts maintained on the cash basis do not disclose the outstanding liabilities of the Government or the arrears of revenue due to it.
2. Under the cash basis, revenues which have accrued but have not been realised are nevertheless fully reflected as assets in the Government accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Cash-basis accounts record only actual receipts and payments, so they do not disclose outstanding liabilities or arrears of revenue due, making statement 1 correct; accrued but unrealised revenues are not reflected as assets, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: 'Commitment accounting', contemplated as part of the reforms towards accrual accounting in Government, involves recording expenditure at the stage when:

options.A: The payment is actually made to the claimant
options.B: The Budget provision for the programme is voted by Parliament
options.C: A commitment or obligation is entered into, such as the placing of an order or the award of a contract, even before the payment falls due
options.D: The Appropriation Accounts of the year are compiled

e: Commitment accounting records expenditure at the stage when a commitment or obligation is entered into, such as placing an order or awarding a contract, even before the payment falls due or is made.

q: Interest received by the Government of India on the loans and advances given by it, such as House Building Advances recovered from Government servants, is classified in the Union Budget as:

options.C: A receipt under the Public Account of India
options.D: A recovery of loans and advances

e: Interest received by the Government of India on loans and advances given by it is a revenue receipt and is classified as non-tax revenue under interest receipts, not as a capital receipt or a recovery of loans.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Loans and advances given by the Government are disbursements of a capital nature which create financial assets for the Government.
2. The interest received on such loans and advances is treated as a capital receipt of the Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Loans and advances given by Government are capital disbursements which create financial assets, so statement 1 is correct; interest on them is revenue (non-tax) receipt, not a capital receipt, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. External grants (aid) received by the Government of India do not create any liability for repayment.
2. External loans received by the Government of India form part of its external debt.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: External grants or aid received by the Government of India are non-repayable and create no liability, while external loans form part of its external debt, so both statements are correct.

q: Loans given by the Government of India to the State Governments are accounted for in the accounts of the Union under:

options.A: The Revenue section of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: The 'Loans and Advances' section of the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Loans given by the Government of India to State Governments are capital disbursements accounted for in the Loans and Advances section of the Consolidated Fund of India, under Major Head 7601.

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government of India for a year is financed mainly through:

options.A: The balances held in the Public Account of India alone
options.B: Market borrowings and dated securities, securities issued against small savings collections, external borrowings and other debt receipts
options.D: The appropriations made to the railway reserve funds

e: The fiscal deficit is financed mainly through debt receipts: market borrowings and dated securities, securities issued against small savings collections, external borrowings and other debt receipts.

q: 'Dated securities' issued by the Government of India are:

options.A: Long-term market loans of the Government with a fixed maturity and coupon, as distinct from Treasury Bills
options.B: Treasury Bills issued for short periods to meet temporary mismatches of cash flow
options.C: Securities issued by the Government to the National Small Savings Fund
options.D: Ways and Means Advances obtained from the Reserve Bank of India

e: Dated securities are the long-term market loans of the Government with a fixed maturity and coupon, as distinct from Treasury Bills which are short-term instruments for temporary cash-flow mismatches.

q: A State Government, in addition to its normal Ways and Means Advances from the Reserve Bank of India, avails of a further facility against the collateral of its Government securities and dated securities held by it. This facility is the:
e: The facility availed by a State Government from the Reserve Bank in addition to normal Ways and Means Advances, against the collateral of its Government securities and dated securities held by it, is the Special Drawing Facility.

q: In a period of economic slowdown, the Government deliberately increases its capital expenditure and allows the fiscal deficit to widen, so as to sustain demand in the economy, intending to consolidate when growth revives. This is an instance of:
e: Deliberately raising capital expenditure and widening the fiscal deficit in a slowdown to sustain demand, with consolidation intended when growth revives, is counter-cyclical fiscal policy, the opposite of pro-cyclical policy.

q: 'Tax expenditure' of the Government refers to:

options.A: The expenditure incurred by the Government on the collection of taxes
options.B: The salary bill of the revenue departments of the Government
options.C: The arrears of taxes outstanding against assessees
options.D: The revenue forgone by the Government on account of the exemptions, deductions and incentives allowed under the tax laws

e: Tax expenditure means the revenue forgone by the Government on account of exemptions, deductions and incentives allowed under the tax laws, shown in the Budget as a statement of revenue forgone.

q: The Output-Outcome Monitoring Framework, under which Government schemes are monitored along with the Budget, seeks primarily to:

options.A: Measure the outputs delivered and the outcomes achieved by schemes against the financial outlays provided for them
options.B: Fix the rates of interest payable on the market borrowings of the Government
options.C: Compile the Finance Accounts of the Union Government
options.D: Determine the share of the States in the divisible pool of taxes

e: The Output-Outcome Monitoring Framework, presented along with the Budget, seeks primarily to measure the outputs delivered and the outcomes achieved by Government schemes against the financial outlays provided for them.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Outputs' of a scheme are its immediate deliverables, such as the assets created or the services delivered by it.
2. 'Outcomes' of a scheme are the effects or results flowing from those deliverables, such as the improvement in the condition sought to be addressed by the scheme.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Outputs of a scheme are its immediate deliverables, such as assets created or services delivered, while outcomes are the effects or results flowing from them, such as improvement in the condition addressed, so both statements are correct.

q: Under a Government scheme, all the physical assets targeted for the year have been created and the services delivered, but there is no measurable improvement in the condition the scheme was meant to improve. The correct assessment is that:

options.A: Both the outputs and the outcomes of the scheme have been achieved
options.B: The outputs have been achieved, but the outcomes have not been achieved
options.C: Neither the outputs nor the outcomes have been achieved
options.D: The outcomes have been achieved, but the outputs have not been achieved

e: Physical assets created and services delivered mean the outputs have been achieved, but with no measurable improvement in the condition the scheme meant to improve, the outcomes have not been achieved, so option B is the correct assessment.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the external debt of the Central Government is accounted for under Major Head:
e: In the classification of Government accounts, the external debt of the Central Government is accounted for under Major Head 6002, in the series 6001 Internal Debt of the Central Government, 6002 External Debt, 6003 and 6004 for States.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the State Provident Funds are accounted for under Major Head:
e: State Provident Funds, forming part of the Public Account of India under Small Savings, Provident Funds etc., are accounted for under Major Head 8009.

q: Personal Deposit accounts maintained in Government accounts form part of the Public Account of India under Major Head:
e: Personal Deposit accounts are maintained under Major Head 8443 Civil Deposits in the Public Account of India, as Minor Head 106 Personal Deposits; Major Head 8336 relates to deposits under the old classification and is not the operative head.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, loans to Government servants, such as House Building Advance and Motor Car Advance, are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Loans to Government servants, such as House Building Advance and Motor Car Advance, are accounted for under Major Head 7610 Loans to Government Servants etc., in the Loans and Advances section.

q: Which one of the following is a section (sector) of the Public Account of India in the Government system of accounts?

options.B: Loans and Advances by the Central Government

e: Remittances is a section of the Public Account of India, along with Debt (other than Consolidated Fund), Deposits and Advances, Suspense and Miscellaneous, and Cash Balance; Public Debt and Loans and Advances belong to the Consolidated Fund.

q: In the Government system of accounts, the Inter-State Suspense Account, through which transactions between States awaiting settlement are adjusted, is Major Head:
e: The Inter-State Suspense Account, through which transactions between States awaiting settlement are adjusted, is Major Head 8793 in the Remittances section of the Public Account.

q: The 'guarantee fee' levied by the Government in respect of the guarantees given by it is:

options.A: The interest charged on the loans guaranteed by the Government
options.B: The amount charged by the Government from the beneficiary for extending its guarantee and bearing the contingent risk on the loan guaranteed
options.C: A deposit taken from the lender before the guarantee is given
options.D: The commission paid by the Government to the Reserve Bank of India for managing the loan

e: Guarantee fee is the amount charged by the Government from the beneficiary for extending its guarantee and bearing the contingent risk on the loan guaranteed; it is not interest on the loan or a commission to the Reserve Bank.

q: The Inter-State Council, which may be established to inquire into and advise upon disputes and matters of common interest between the States and the Union, is provided for in the Constitution under:
e: The Inter-State Council is provided for in Article 263 of the Constitution, which empowers the President to establish such a Council to inquire into and advise upon inter-State disputes and matters of common interest.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, 'Appropriation for reduction or avoidance of Debt' of the Central Government is accounted for under Major Head:
e: Appropriation for reduction or avoidance of Debt of the Central Government is accounted for under Major Head 2048, distinct from Major Head 2049 Interest Payments and Major Head 6001 Internal Debt.

q: In performance audit, the 'criteria' against which the performance of a programme is assessed are:

options.A: The benchmarks, standards or expectations, derived from laws, rules, stated objectives and sound practice, against which the actual performance is compared
options.B: The replies furnished by the audited entity to the audit findings
options.C: The monetary value of the transactions test-checked in audit
options.D: The recommendations made in the earlier reports of the Public Accounts Committee

e: In performance audit, criteria are the benchmarks, standards or expectations, derived from laws, rules, stated objectives and sound practice, against which the actual performance of a programme is compared and assessed.

q: In the classification of Government accounts, 'General Services', 'Social Services' and 'Economic Services' are examples of:
e: General Services, Social Services and Economic Services are the sectors (sectoral classification) under which the Major Heads of Government accounts are grouped, above the level of Major Heads in the classification hierarchy.

q: In the six-tier classification of Government accounts, a Sub-Major Head under a Major Head represents:

options.A: A programme undertaken to achieve the objectives of the function
options.C: The object of the expenditure, such as salaries or travel expenses
options.D: A sub-function of the Government within the major function represented by the Major Head

e: In the six-tier classification, a Sub-Major Head under a Major Head represents a sub-function of Government within the major function represented by the Major Head; programmes, schemes and objects come at the lower tiers.

q:
Consider the following statements about the 'just-in-time' release of funds for Centrally Sponsored Schemes through Single Nodal Agency accounts:
1. Funds are released to the implementing agencies only as and when they are actually required for expenditure, so as to avoid the parking of Government funds outside the Government account and the interest cost of idle balances.
2. Under this system, the entire annual allocation is advanced to the implementing agencies in a lump sum at the beginning of the financial year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Under just-in-time release through Single Nodal Agency accounts, funds are released to implementing agencies only as and when actually required, avoiding parking of funds outside the Government account and interest cost on idle balances, so statement 1 is correct and statement 2, describing lump-sum advance, is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Money should not be drawn from the Consolidated Fund of India unless it is required for immediate disbursement.
2. Money may properly be drawn in advance merely to prevent the lapse of a grant and parked in a deposit or Personal Deposit account for use in the following year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Money should not be drawn from the Consolidated Fund unless required for immediate disbursement, so statement 1 is correct; drawing money in advance merely to prevent lapse of a grant and parking it in a deposit or Personal Deposit account is expressly prohibited, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: The debt of a Government is regarded as sustainable when:

options.A: The Government borrows only from external sources
options.B: The Government can continue to service its debt without requiring an unrealistically large future correction in its revenues and expenditure
options.C: The fiscal deficit of the Government is exactly equal to its interest payments
options.D: The entire borrowing of the year is used for meeting the revenue deficit

e: Government debt is sustainable when the Government can continue to service its debt without requiring an unrealistically large future correction in the balance of revenues and non-debt expenditure.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deposits accounted for in the Public Account of India are classified into deposits bearing interest and deposits not bearing interest.
2. All deposits held in the Public Account of India necessarily bear interest payable by the Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Deposits in the Public Account are classified into deposits bearing interest and deposits not bearing interest, so statement 1 is correct; not all deposits bear interest, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: The investment of the cash balances of the Government of India, made through the Reserve Bank of India, is accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head:
e: The investment of the cash balances of the Government of India, made through the Reserve Bank of India, is accounted for in the Public Account under Major Head 8673 Cash Balance Investment Account.

q: In the Government system of accounts, transactions relating to money orders are accounted for under Major Head:

options.A: 8786 – Adjusting Account between Central and State Governments

e: Transactions relating to money orders in Government accounts are accounted for under Major Head 8781 Money Orders, in the Remittances section of the Public Account of India.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, Insurance and Pension Funds are accounted for under Major Head:
e: Insurance and Pension Funds in the Public Account of India are accounted for under Major Head 8011, in the Small Savings, Provident Funds etc. sector along with 8009 State Provident Funds.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, the General and Other Reserve Funds of the Central Government are accounted for under Major Head:
e: The General and Other Reserve Funds of the Central Government are accounted for under Major Head 8121 in the Reserve Funds section of the Public Account of India.

q: Deposits of Local Funds, such as the funds of local bodies placed in Government treasuries, are accounted for in the Public Account of India under Major Head:
e: Deposits of Local Funds, such as funds of local bodies placed in Government treasuries, are accounted for in the Public Account under Major Head 8448 Deposits of Local Funds, distinct from 8443 Civil Deposits.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, Major Head 8550 relates to:
e: Major Head 8550 in the Public Account of India relates to Civil Advances, in the Advances section along with Defence, Railway, Postal and Telecommunication Advances.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The internal debt and the external debt of the Central Government are accounted for in the Public Debt section of the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Public Debt forms part of the Public Account of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Internal and external debt of the Central Government are accounted for in the Public Debt section of the Consolidated Fund of India, so statement 1 is correct; Public Debt is not part of the Public Account, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Reserve Funds maintained in the Public Account of India:
1. Reserve Funds are classified into Reserve Funds bearing interest and Reserve Funds not bearing interest.
2. Every Reserve Fund maintained in the Public Account of India necessarily bears interest payable by the Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Reserve Funds in the Public Account are classified into Reserve Funds bearing interest and Reserve Funds not bearing interest, so statement 1 is correct; every Reserve Fund does not necessarily bear interest, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A surcharge levied by the Union under Article 271 of the Constitution forms part of the Consolidated Fund of India but is not shared with the States.
2. A cess levied for a specific purpose is excluded from the divisible pool of taxes shareable with the States.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: A surcharge under Article 271 forms part of the Consolidated Fund of India but is excluded from the divisible pool shared with the States, and a cess levied for a specific purpose is likewise excluded from the divisible pool under Article 270, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Contingency Fund of India:
1. The Fund is administered by the Secretary in the Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs) on behalf of the President of India.
2. Every advance out of the Fund requires the prior approval of the Lok Sabha before it is made.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: The Contingency Fund of India under Article 267 is administered by the Secretary, Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs) on behalf of the President, so statement 1 is correct; advances are made without prior Lok Sabha approval and are later recouped after authorisation, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: In audit terminology, expenditure incurred without any provision in the grant or appropriation for the purpose, as distinct from expenditure incurred without the sanction of the competent authority, is termed as:
e: In audit terminology, expenditure incurred without any provision in the grant or appropriation is unauthorised expenditure, whereas expenditure without the sanction of the competent authority is unsanctioned expenditure.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Funds once surrendered out of a grant cannot be re-appropriated later in the same financial year.
2. Savings surrendered out of a grant remain available to the executive for meeting an excess under another grant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Funds once surrendered out of a grant cannot be re-appropriated later in the same financial year, so statement 1 is correct; surrendered savings lapse and are not available to the executive for meeting excess under another grant, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: Re-appropriation of funds within a grant is NOT permissible where its effect would be:

options.A: To meet an anticipated excess under a sub-head from savings available under another sub-head of the same grant
options.B: To augment the provision for an item of expenditure which Parliament has deliberately reduced by adopting a cut motion
options.C: To provide for an item of expenditure already covered by the grant
options.D: To adjust the provision between two units of appropriation within the same grant

e: Re-appropriation is not permissible to augment provision for an item of expenditure which Parliament has deliberately reduced by adopting a cut motion, as that would defeat the will of Parliament expressed in the vote.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'new instrument of service' from a 'new service'?

options.A: A new instrument of service is a new form or head of expenditure arising under an existing service, as from a change of policy or practice, while a new service is expenditure on a purpose or service not contemplated in the Budget at all
options.B: A new service is a new form of expenditure under an existing service, while a new instrument of service is a wholly new purpose not contemplated in the Budget
options.C: There is no difference between the two expressions
options.D: A new instrument of service relates only to charged expenditure, while a new service relates only to voted expenditure

e: A new service is expenditure on a purpose or service not contemplated in the Budget at all, while a new instrument of service is a new form or head of expenditure arising under an existing service, as from a change of policy or practice, so option A states the distinction correctly.

q: The Appropriation Accounts of a grant bring out, among other things:

options.A: Only the total savings under the grant for the year
options.B: The Profit and Loss Account of the department concerned
options.C: The excesses over the grant which require regularisation by Parliament through Excess Grants
options.D: The arrears of revenue due to the Government

e: The Appropriation Accounts of a grant bring out, among other things, the excesses over the grant or appropriation which require regularisation by Parliament through Excess Grants under Article 115.

q: A Financial Bill of the first category, containing matters specified in Article 110 together with other matters, differs from a Money Bill in that:

options.A: It can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha also
options.B: It does not require the recommendation of the President for its introduction
options.C: It can be introduced only by a private member
options.D: The Rajya Sabha can amend or reject it, and a joint sitting of the two Houses can be held in case of disagreement

e: A Financial Bill of the first category, containing Article 110 matters together with other matters, can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha like a Money Bill, but unlike a Money Bill the Rajya Sabha can amend or reject it and a joint sitting can be held on disagreement.

q: Consequent upon the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the Demands for Grants of the Railways are presented to Parliament:

options.A: As sixteen separate Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways, as before the merger
options.B: As a single Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways forming part of the Union Budget
options.C: Only through the Finance Bill of the year
options.D: As charged expenditure, without any Demand being presented

e: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the Demands for Grants of Railways are presented as a single Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways forming part of the Union Budget, instead of sixteen separate Demands as before.
